narrative.overview: Charta is a print studio's proofing table rendered in software: warm uncoated paper, dense black ink, and on the table the client's work, which is the only thing allowed to be in colour.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper neutrals (hue 85) and warm ink (hue 60), never pure white or pure black.
Colour in the interface comes from the user's brand only; chrome stays achromatic-warm.
Brand previews always sit on neutral grey with zero chroma.
Pill controls, 16 to 24 px sheets, hairline borders, soft ambient shadows.

rules.name: The Client Owns Colour Rule
rules.body: No saturated colour in the chrome. Saturated colour on screen is either the user's brand or a status, and nothing else.

rules.name: The Grey Light Box Rule
rules.body: A brand colour or logo is only ever previewed on preview-grey (chroma 0) or on a surface the user chose, never on the warm paper.

rules.name: The Evidence Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Any computed value (colour code, ratio, size, time) is set in Geist Mono with tabular figures. Prose never contains a raw measurement in the body font.

rules.name: The Paper Weight Rule
rules.body: Only things that represent a printed artefact (sheets, mockups) or float above the work cast a shadow. Panels and cards do not.

dos: Do keep the interface to paper, ink and status colours; let the user's brand provide all other colour.
Do preview every logo and swatch on preview-grey.
Do set every measured value in Geist Mono with tabular figures.
Do keep one primary ink button per screen.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: skeletons and reveals fall back to instant states.
donts: Don't use pure white #FFFFFF or pure black #000000 in the chrome.
Don't give the interface its own brand accent colour.
Don't put a shadow on panels or inspector cards.
Don't show raw JSON or event codes to the user; the journal speaks in sentences.
